title: Noise contracts the extended functional
statement: Let $n,m\ge0$ and $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous on $[0,1]$ and nonnegative there. Suppose that whenever $a+b,a-b\in[0,1]$, $P(a)\le\bigl(\sqrt{P(a+b)^2+b^2}+\sqrt{P(a-b)^2+b^2}\bigr)/2$. For any real-valued functions $f,g_1,\ldots,g_m$ on $\{0,1\}^n$ with $f(x)\in[0,1]$ for every $x$, and any $\rho\in[0,1]$, the extended functional satisfies $F_P(T_\rho f,(T_\rho g_j)_j)\le F_P(f,(g_j)_j)$, where $T_\rho$ is the Fourier noise operator.
hypotheses_covered: the stated two-point inequality holds whenever $a\pm b\in[0,1]$
$f$ is a real-valued function on $\{0,1\}^n$ with values in $[0,1]$
$g$ is an $m$-tuple of real-valued functions on $\{0,1\}^n$
replaced: For $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and $g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ of real functions on the cube, write $V(f,g)(x)=(D_1f(x),\ldots,D_nf(x),g_1(x),\ldots,g_m(x))$ and $F_P(f,g)=\mathbb E\sqrt{P(f)^2+\|V(f,g)\|_2^2}$, with $D_i$ the coordinate half-difference. Assume $P\ge0$ on $[0,1]$ and, whenever $z\pm d\in[0,1]$, $P(z)\le\bigl(\sqrt{P(z+d)^2+d^2}+\sqrt{P(z-d)^2+d^2}\bigr)/2$. If $P$ is continuous on $[0,1]$, $f$ takes values in $[0,1]$, and $0\le\rho\le1$, then $F_P(T_\rho f,T_\rho g)\le F_P(f,g)$, where $T_\rho$ is Boolean noise applied to each component.
